Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NimbusCloud Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing NimbusCloud's results for the Q3 2024. With me on the call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Product Officer; Taylor Brooks, Chief Marketing Officer; Chris Ramirez, Chief Sales Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Security Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. NimbusCloud delivered exceptional results for the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our cloud platform and the increasing demand for our AI-driven solutions across diverse industries.

During the quarter, we focused on eight key strategic priorities:
1. Expanding our global reach through strategic partnerships.
2. Driving innovation in edge computing and IoT solutions.
3. Enhancing our commitment to open source technologies.
4. Strengthening our data privacy and compliance programs.
5. Investing in our employees' professional development.
6. Improving our operational efficiency through automation.
7. Fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.
8. Accelerating the adoption of sustainable cloud practices.

These priorities have directly fueled our cost optimization initiatives, which have become a cornerstone of our operational excellence strategy this year. In the hyperscale cloud environment, where we compete head-to-head with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform on price-performance, controlling costs is essential not just for margins but for sustaining aggressive pricing to capture market share in the maturing IaaS and PaaS landscape. We've achieved tangible results, including an 18% year-over-year reduction in our cost of revenues as a percentage of total revenue, which has driven our adjusted EBITDA margins to 32%, up 450 basis points from Q3 2023.

Key pillars include infrastructure efficiency, procurement and supply chain levers, and AI/ML-driven automation. On infrastructure, we've pursued rightsizing and workload optimization across our 42 global regions. Rightsizing alone—migrating underutilized instances equivalent to EC2 from high-cost types to more efficient Graviton-based ARM instances—generated $285 million in annualized savings. We've also seen a 25% uptake in our Spot Instance program, where customers such as our top financial services client, a leading bulge-bracket bank, shifted 40% of non-critical batch workloads to spot pricing, providing us with an effective 65% discount on compute costs during peak hours.

Advanced tools like our Nimbus AutoScaler, using reinforcement learning models trained on petabytes of historical telemetry data, have reduced idle capacity by 22%, especially for Kubernetes-orchestrated container workloads on our EKS-like service. For storage, our S3-compatible object store achieved a 15% OpEx reduction via intelligent tiering algorithms that move cold data to our Glacier Deep Archive equivalent, cutting access costs by 60% for archival workloads. Amid the AI boom, GPU optimization has been transformative: dynamic slicing on our A100/H100 clusters, similar to AWS Trainium or Azure's NDv5 series, boosted utilization from 55% to 82%, saving $120 million in the quarter while supporting a 3x ramp in inference workloads for GenAI customers.

Procurement-wise, long-term commitments with suppliers like NVIDIA and custom silicon partners secured volume discounts averaging 28% on next-gen TPUs and NPUs. We've diversified from legacy x86, with ARM-based instances now at 35% of our fleet—echoing Google Cloud trends—and this cut per-core CapEx by 12%. Data center buildouts stay disciplined: we delayed $400 million in secondary market greenfield expansions, favoring edge colocation with Equinix and Digital Realty, which improved our power usage effectiveness to 1.18 globally from 1.25 last year.

Regionally, impacts vary. North America, 52% of revenue, saw 20% YoY decline in unit economics from hyperscale density in Virginia and Oregon zones, countering AWS dominance. EMEA gained 24% savings via renewable energy PPAs in Frankfurt and Paris; with EU energy spikes of 15% from geopolitical tensions, our 85% renewable mix kept us 30% below peers. APAC cut costs 16% through sovereign clouds in Mumbai and Jakarta, using cheaper hydro power and reducing data egress by 40% for intra-region traffic. LatAm, 8% of revenue, benefited from fiber expansions with Telefónica, trimming latency overprovisioning by 18%.

These aren't one-offs; they're part of our Cloud Efficiency Engine framework, integrating FinOps with real-time cost allocation via Nimbus Cost Explorer. This improved customer TCO by 28% on average, per Forrester benchmarks, winning 15% more RFPs against Azure in hybrid multi-cloud deals. We're reinvesting 10% of savings—about $750 million annually—into R&D for quantum-resistant encryption and photonic interconnects, setting us up for post-Moore's Law. Margins should expand 200 basis points in FY25 as AI scales. Even with 10% energy spikes or chip shortages, our stack holds 30%+ EBITDA.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Patel to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Michael Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue increased by 28% year-over-year to $2.9 billion, exceeding our guidance for the quarter. Our gross margin was 68.7%, driven by our efficient cost management and economies of scale. Our operating margin was 32%.

Before moving on, let me address the expected impact of macroeconomic factors on our outlook. As a leading hyperscale cloud provider, with over 45% of our trailing twelve-month revenue from enterprise AI/ML, SaaS migrations, and hybrid cloud, we're well-positioned but watchful of inflation, high interest rates, currency volatility, and uneven demand.

In the U.S., 52% of run-rate revenue, inflation at 3.1% CPI has core services pressuring costs. Data center electricity, 15% of opex, rose 12% YoY in Virginia and Oregon from droughts and GPU ramps. Our $2.5 billion renewable PPAs secure 75% U.S. power from solar/wind by year-end, stabilizing margins at 28-30% for FY24, down slightly from 32%.

Interest rates, Fed at 4.75-5% through mid-2025 per CME, raised debt costs 150 bps on our $10B term loan to 4.8% from 3.2%. This curbs customer capex; 68% of Fortune 1000 CIOs defer on-prem, favoring our consumption model. RPO grew 22% YoY to $45B, 65% multi-year, but we guide FY24 revenue to 16-18%, trimmed 200 bps for non-AI slowdown.

AI tailwinds shine: CloudForge AI Foundry-like platform with H100s and liquid-cooled Nx64 saw AI compute up 45% QoQ to 28% revenue. Sticky inference like JPMorgan fraud pilots and HIPAA fine-tuning win share.

EMEA, 22% revenue, faces ECB hawkishness and energy shocks. German industrials cut 8% commitments with PMI <45; EUR/USD down 12% shaved 90 bps growth. Frankfurt/Paris sovereign zones with Kyber-1024 quantum-safe gain GDPR traction; expect 12-14% FY24 growth, margins +150 bps to 72% via 5G MEC with Vodafone/Deutsche Telekom.

APAC, 18%, bifurcated: Japan/ANZ robust at 65% adoption, Tokyo-3 for Sony/Toyota sims up 25% YoY. China capped 5%, soft 10-15%; $1.2B in Graviton4 cuts NVIDIA reliance 20%. FX headwind 3% from USD strength, hedged 55% locally, limits EBITDA hit to 1.5%.

Resilience via Cloud Economics Optimizer for 25-30% savings, NRR 118% > peers; ForgeBridge for hybrid; carbon-aware scheduling for CSRD/ESG. Macro fricts 2-3 pts growth, but AI moat/consumption yields 16-18% revenue, 28-30% margins, $8.5-9B FCF FY24.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology strategy and roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. We are committed to leading the way in cloud technology innovation. We are making significant investments in research and development to create cutting-edge solutions for our customers.

A key focus is our compute and storage capacity utilization rates, vital for infrastructure efficiency and scaling AI/enterprise workloads like GenAI training on Nova GPU clusters or petabyte data lakes.

For Q3, overall compute utilization across x86, Arm NovaPrime, and accelerators hit 84%, +450 bps QoQ from 79.5%, +1200 bps YoY from 72%—our highest in two years, thanks to capacity planning and hyperscale demand.

By category: General-purpose (On-Demand/Spot Nova) at 82%, from 28% YoY Reserved Instance uptick, Fortune 500 VMware migrations; burstable CI/CD with auto-scaling rightsizing t4g.mediums.

AI/ML accelerators at 91%, +6% QoQ; Llama 3/StratoLLM inference extends H100 jobs to 48 hours/pod, beating AWS Trainium by 300 bps.

Storage blended 76%, +320 bps QoQ/+950 bps YoY: Object (60% capacity) 78% with tiering to StratoVault at 92%; block 71% from e-commerce databases, offset by snapshots.

Regionally: North America (52% revenue) 87%, Meta/OpenAI colos in Virginia/Oregon; EMEA 81%, SAP HANA finance in Frankfurt; APAC 79% +1800 bps YoY, 5G edge Japan/India; LatAm 72%, São Paulo targeting 80%.

Drivers: StratoOptimizer AI (Q1 launch) analyzes 1.5T API calls for migrations c5.xlarge to c6g, 15% recapture, 65% top adoption; hypervisor packing +22% density on Arm; PUE 1.18 liquid-cooled; Spot/Savings 35% demand at 70% off.

Efficiency First capex: $12.4B FY24 down 8%/TB; project Q4 compute 88%, storage 80% mid-2025 with 25% AI growth. Beats Azure 78%; funds Quantum-Ready fabric despite GPU delays/EU regs.

Now, I'll pass it over to Jordan Lee to discuss our product roadmap and recent launches.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Elena. We recently launched NimbusEdge, a groundbreaking solution designed to revolutionize edge computing for IoT and low-latency AI applications.

Our data center expansions and capex updates underpin this roadmap. Explosive GenAI, sovereign cloud, hybrid/edge demand drives our hyperscale scaling for the multi-trillion TAM, optimized for efficiency/sustainability/latency.

Q3 FY2024 capex $12.4B, +48% YoY/+22% QoQ; TTM $48.7B, FY guide $52-56B. 72% ($8.9B) PP&E data centers/servers; 18% ($2.2B) networking; 10% R&D liquid GPU.

On track 1.2 GW incremental to 8.5 GW/38 AZ/18 regions, +35% YoY >25-30% industry.

North America: 200 MW Virginia facilities, 500 MW Phoenix for AetherAI Fabric H100/Blackwell 10 exaFLOPS; serves Southwest banks/autos at 92% util.

EMEA: Warsaw 150 MW EU-compliant first Eastern Europe; Frankfurt +300 MW quantum-resistant; Paris 5G edge; 22% revenue + from public sector.

APAC: Singapore 400 MW Graviton4; Jakarta 250 MW Q4; TSMC co-lo Taiwan low latency Alibaba/Tencent rivals.

Edge pilots 12 U.S. metros <10 MW AetherEdge Kubernetes serverless AR/VR/IoT.

Innovations: direct-to-chip liquid cooling -40% energy vs air; 50k racks AetherOptic 800G 99.999% SLA <1ms; 65% renewables to 100% 2028, 2.5 GW PPAs.

Ecosystem: AI util 89%, GPU 2x, $500M+ ARR hyperscalers like OpenAI Azure; rev/MW $18.5M > capex/MW $6.2M 3x 24-mo return.

Q4 capex $13.2-13.8B H2 skew; risks ASIC/power mitigated multi-source AMD/Intel Habana/AetherTPU, PPAs. 18% GenAI share per Canalys.

Positions 28-32% growth FY25 $1.2T cloud.

I'll now hand it over to Taylor Brooks to provide an update on our marketing initiatives and brand strategy.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jordan. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and driving demand for our innovative solutions.

Central to this is our customer churn rate and retention trends, showcasing platform stickiness in competing with AWS/Azure/Google Cloud on AI/ML, data lakes, Kubernetes.

Q3 annualized dollar churn 4.2%, -90 bps YoY from 5.1%, lowest in 2+ years; FY guide 4-5% < IDC 6-8% industry.

NRR 118% +6 pts YoY/+3 pts Q1; land-expand.

Gross retention 96.5% multi-year Sovereign/Reserved 40-50% off; logo churn 2.8% mid-market econ; enterprise sub-1%, no top-100 losses.

Enterprise >$1M ARR 122% NRR, 65% Fortune 500 2.5x AI StratoAI; SMB/mid 108% shift to H100s.

Regions: NA 72% ARR 120% NRR <3% churn, multi-cloud vs Outposts/Arc 15% hybrid; EMEA 18% 114% 5.1% churn GDPR, StratoSovereign €200M German auto edge; APAC 10% 125% <3%, Tokyo/Singapore 40% Alibaba cross.

Drivers: ML churn predict 200+ signals K8s/S3 logins 92% accuracy, interventions 48 hrs reclaim $15M ARR; ecosystem Snowflake/Databricks 70% expansions; serverless 3x switching costs; 82% renewals AI usage/evergreen 10-15% uplift 95% 18+ mo advance.

NRR low-120s YE, $2B GPU 1GW 2025; churn FY 4-5% NRR 116-120% 25%+ ARR.

Next, I'd like to introduce Chris Ramirez, who will discuss our sales performance and customer acquisition strategies.

Chris Ramirez:
Thank you, Taylor. Our sales team has been instrumental in driving our strong growth in the Q3. We are focused on expanding our customer base and strengthening our existing relationships.

A critical element is our revenue guidance for the cloud segment and full company next quarter and full year. Cloud 92% revenue Q3, AI/ML/GenAI/sovereign.

Cloud Q4 2025 $2.85-2.95B +24-28% YoY +6-10% QoQ > prior $2.75-2.90B; AetherAI Inference 15% GPUaaS share.

AI/ML compute +35-38% YoY Q4 vs 32% Q3 NexGen T4 Arm > x86 40%; QuantumVector DB 25% GenAI attach.

Storage/data +22% StratoObject zero-ETL Snowflake/Databricks -30% TCO.

Regions: US/Can 55% +26% DoD C2S; APAC 22% +35% Mumbai/Tokyo 95%; EMEA 18% Frankfurt GDPR.

FY2025 cloud $11.6-11.9B +27-31% vs $9.1B FY24; RPO $18.2B +42% 85% 12-mo; ARR $10.8B +29%.

EdgeForge +15 edge Q4 IoT/5G; NVIDIA H200 20% Q4; OpenForge Kubernetes/Anthos hybrid Fortune 500.

Full co Q4 $3.05-3.15B +24-28%; FY $12.4-12.7B +27-31%; services +12% hardware +8%.

Margins cloud 78-79% +150-200 bps silicon/power; opEx 32-33% AI security SentinelGuard.

Risks budget/FX balanced; 75% AI gross top10 <5%; >21% market CAGR Gartner sovereign/agentic AI.

Now, I'll pass it over to Lisa Wong to discuss our security initiatives and commitment to data protection.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Chris. Security is paramount to our mission. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and ensuring the integrity of our cloud platform.

In this context, our geographic revenue breakdown and trends highlight how security enables global growth. Q3 revenue $2.9B +28% YoY +8% QoQ? Wait, template $2.9B +28%, yes. IaaS/PaaS/SaaS AI/edge/sovereign.

Segments: Americas 58% $1.68B +28% YoY +7% QoQ US 92% Virginia/Oregon/Ohio 92% util AI bank GPU like NVIDIA DGX AWS; Can 5% sovereign Digital Charter; LatAm 3% +42% Brazil/Mex AetherEdge 5G Claro/Telefónica; $2.5B Ohio/São Paulo RPO $145B +35%.

EMEA 24% $696M +42% +11% Europe 78% Germany +55% UK +48% Frankfurt/Paris 95% DSGVO AetherSovereign airgap FedRAMP BMW Azure; ME 15% +68% Saudi/UAE Dammam NEOM; Africa 7% +30% MTN edge; energy shift Nordics PUE 1.18 $1.8B Riyadh 35% CAGR Gartner.

APAC 15% $435M +38% +9% Japan/Aus 55% +40/45% Tokyo-3 Sony media; India 20% +62% Reliance Jio 5G PaaS; China 5% Alibaba hybrid; SEA +50% Sing/Indo; AetherKube 60% ARR $12B +50% $1.2B Jakarta 40%+ FY25.

RoW 3% $87M +25% NZ agritech 35% SE Europe sovereign; 65% util RPO $4.5B +28%.

Diversification: Americas 58% -4 pts; EMEA/APAC +3/+2 pts Synergy cloud repatriation pause. AI 28% pipeline +13 pts; edge $250B IDC 2028; residency regs.

45 regions/150+ edge Aether Fabric SDN <50ms > OVH/Huawei; NRR 128% 65% greenfield hyperscalers; FX 3% energy hedge 70% renewable.

Q4 geo +30-35% APAC/EMEA 40%+; $15B capex 45% int'l 20 new DCs AI zones $1T TAM McKinsey 2030.

Finally, I'd like to introduce Raj Singh, who will share insights into our innovation strategy and future growth opportunities.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Lisa. We are constantly exploring new technologies and business models to drive innovation and create value for our customers.

Our overall gross margin trends and drivers exemplify this innovation impact. Q3 68.7% +150 bps YoY from 67.2% +20 bps QoQ; 11th straight expansion, TTM 68.2% > peer 66% Synergy; 5-yr from 62.4% FY19 hyperscale/product mix.

Service mix tailwind: AI/ML/analytics/NexAI/managed DB 28% rev +6 pts >75% margins > IaaS 65%; GenAI +140% NVIDIA H100/Blackwell NexCore V2 ARM like Trainium/Maia; legacy storage/compute 15% mix down.

Data center ops leverage: 87% util +5 pts ML rack forecast; PUE 1.14 liquid 40% new 60% renewable PPAs Texas/Nordics -12% energy YoY +8% prices; SDN -15% bandwidth 25% egress surge.

Regions: Americas 52% 70.2% Virginia/Oregon SAP NexCloud; EMEA 68.9% Frankfurt/Paris sovereign; APAC 22% 65.4% Alibaba/Tencent pricing Japan/India fabs +300 bps Singapore scale.

Headwinds: Azure bundling -2-3% IaaS NRR 112% upsell; AI capex $2.1B GPU +50 bps frontloaded 20-30% throughput/watt.

Sustain +100 bps annual: NexCore V3 Q4 2x inference >80%; Cost Opt Hub 65% top $500M savings auto/spot; Dell edge telco 5G 72%; low-carbon tier 1-2% ESG.

Q4 68.9-69.3% FY24 68.5% FY25 AI 35% util >90% > AWS 67.8% GCP 66.5% R&D no dilution.

Back to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term sustainable growth.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Can you elaborate on how your cost optimization is positioning you against hyperscalers in AI pricing wars, and any updates on customer wins from those savings?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, John. Our cost optimizations, as I detailed, directly enable competitive pricing while expanding margins. The $285M savings from rightsizing and 82% GPU util have let us offer better TCO, winning 15% more RFPs versus Azure. Key wins include expanding with our bulge-bracket bank on spot workloads and new GenAI inference deals, solidifying our price-performance edge.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great results. On capex and data center expansions, how are you managing supply chain risks for GPUs and power in new regions like APAC?

Michael Patel:
Thanks, Emily. We've mitigated via multi-sourcing—AMD, Intel Habana, in-house AetherTPU—and long-term NVIDIA reservations. Power via 15-year PPAs, 65% renewables. In APAC, TSMC co-lo and Jakarta hydro keep us on track for 1.2 GW add, with rev/MW efficiency at 3x return.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Impressive NRR and churn metrics. What's driving the APAC outperformance in retention, and outlook for sovereign cloud there?

Raj Singh:
David, thanks. APAC NRR 125% from GenAI demand Japan/India, integrations like Alibaba cross-flows, and sovereign zones Mumbai/Jakarta cutting egress 40%. Churn sub-3%; sovereign pilots expanding with data localization, targeting 40%+ growth FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
On compute utilization, with 91% on GPUs, how sustainable is that amid Blackwell delays, and impact on guidance?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Rachel, solid question. 91% driven by inference stickiness and StratoOptimizer recapture; sustainable via packing algos and spot filling troughs. NVIDIA delays hedged with multi-ASIC; supports Q4 88% compute, AI accel in guidance.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions and your continued interest in NimbusCloud.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
